issues.description: The problem statement initially requires a modifiable List<Meal> for the orders attribute, but later text and the provided solution/template use and expect an array-based orders representation. This contradiction (List vs array) is structural and will confuse students about which data structure to implement and which helpers (ArrayHelpers) to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either require an array-backed orders attribute (e.g., Meal[] orders) throughout the problem statement and note use of ArrayHelpers, or update the template and solution to use List<Meal> (and adjust ArrayHelpers/tests accordingly). Preferably, update problem_statement.md to request a Meal[] orders array to match the provided ArrayHelpers and the solution.

issues.description: The problem statement describes the exercise as 'Panic at Seal Saloon' (Seal Saloon theme), while the project root names in the provided repositories refer to 'Panic-at-Burger-House' (template) and 'Panic-at-Burger-House-Solution' (solution). This mismatch in the exercise/project naming (exercise title vs. repository project name) refers to the same conceptual entity (the exercise/theme) with different identifiers across artifacts and may cause avoidable confusion for students about which exercise they are working on.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the exercise/project naming across artifacts. For example, update the template and solution settings.gradle rootProject.name to reference 'H02E02---Panic-at-Seal-Saloon' (or adjust the problem statement to match the repository name) so the exercise title/theme is consistent in the problem text and both repositories.
